source.title: Learning from Noisy Labels for Entity-Centric Information Extraction

record.tranche_reason: Tests performance under synthetic label noise on NLP information extraction datasets, extending the noisy-label question to a new task and modality.
record.gate_note: The study tests synthetic label-flip rates and reports test F1. It does not report training error on random labels, chance-level test error, or training-time comparisons. Statements about memorization and learning noisy labels in the introduction and related work cite prior studies and are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study supplies new NLP results bearing on V4's test-performance trend and V6's learning order. Table 7 measures generalization as label corruption increases. Section 4.5 additionally reports that performance against corrected labels on training instances first rises and then falls, which the authors explicitly interpret as delayed learning of noise. Neither experiment establishes perfect training-set memorization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the synthetic-noise experiment. More broadly, the authors conclude that agreement-based co-regularization improves noisy-label IE training, with lower computational cost than CrossWeigh. Their own noise-filtering analysis also reports an initial rise followed by a fall in corrected-label F1, consistent with delayed noise learning; the record overlooks this result.
record.recipe_differences: NLP entity-centric information extraction with synthetic label flipping and test F1 evaluation; the study does not reproduce the original image-classification random-label experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset/task (TACRED relation extraction and CoNLL03 named entity recognition); synthetic label-flip rate; model and co-regularization configuration.

fits_no_version.finding: Co-regularization outperforms the base model and CrossWeigh at every tested synthetic corruption rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Co-regularization improves noise-robust relation-extraction performance relative to these comparison methods.

fits_no_version.finding: Test F1 decreases as increasing fractions of flipped-label instances are removed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reducing the available training data degrades TACRED generalization in this control.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The synthetic-noise sweep reports test F1 rather than training error; it tests rates only from 10% to 90%, not complete random labeling. The supplied text does not report uncertainty intervals for Table 7.

untested.parts: Complete random labeling, zero or near-zero training error, chance test error, and fitting without architecture or hyperparameter changes.
Relative time to fit true versus random labels and convergence speed across corruption fractions. Computational comparisons between denoising methods do not test this.

Perfect training fit throughout the corruption sweep; a fully clean starting dataset; 100% corruption; a chance-performance endpoint; and simultaneous measurement of signal learning and noise memorization.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization. The proposed agreement loss does not test those interventions.

Direct, separate accuracy or loss trajectories against clean and noisy training labels, and completely random-label learning. Figure 2 supplies indirect evidence from corrected-label F1 rather than a direct noisy-label memorization curve.

missing.what: Learning trajectories for C-GCN and BERTBASE on 2,526 known mislabeled instances included in training, scored against corrected labels. Record the stated initial rise and subsequent fall in F1, separating gamma=0 baselines from co-regularized conditions. Exact curve values cannot be recovered from the supplied text.

No-additional-flipping reference results on the relabeled TACRED test set: BERTBASE 76.9, CrossWeigh 79.1, and CR 80.0 F1. These are references on the original noisy training set, not clean-label baselines.

record.verdict_notes: Observed states for R1–R15 refer only to V4's measured generalization trend, not its unmeasured perfect-training-fit component. Missing training-fit measurements do not justify limits_scope or challenges. The original TACRED training labels already contain natural noise, and zero relation-extraction F1 does not establish chance-level classification.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labeling, training error, chance-level test error, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Training-time cost and convergence speed as corruption increases.
Shuffled pixels, permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.

The study reports test F1 under 10%–90% synthetic label flipping, but does not report whether training error remains perfect, does not test 100% corruption, and does not establish the version's proposed mechanism of capturing remaining signal while memorizing noise.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation affect fitting random labels or true-label generalization.
Whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels, or whether their learning differs over training.
